problem: LVLM navigation agents are mostly trained by imitating a single expert trajectory (R2R/RxR-style), which gives only sparse, binary supervision and ignores alternative valid routes, so agents memorize paths instead of learning to compare actions.
motivation: Goal-driven navigation (ObjectNav / instance-image-goal) has many valid paths and needs exploration under uncertainty. Modular map-based systems are fragile to sensor noise, while end-to-end LVLMs trained by imitation generalize poorly. The paper wants the agent to evaluate the relative value of all candidate actions rather than replicate one path.
key_idea: Replace path imitation with decision understanding: annotate every candidate action with A* geodesic distance to the goal, and train a Qwen2.5-VL-7B with SFT-then-GRPO using a gap-aware hybrid reward that is decisive when the best action is clearly better and soft when options are close.
insight: Dense per-action distances, converted to a softmax base score plus a certainty-gated bonus, give a more useful RL signal than binary or min-max rewards (reward ablation: Binary 29.5 / Min-Max 29.2 / Ours 35.6 SR on InsImageNav). SFT warm-up is essential: RFT from scratch gives 23.5 SR versus 35.6 from SFT. Binary and min-max rewards reach higher training reward but generalize worse, which suggests they only teach mimicry of the single best action.
method: Compass-Data-RFT: an Action Proposal Module (VLMNav-style, from depth and occupancy) proposes candidate polar actions (r,θ) drawn as arrows; an oracle A* annotator in habitat-sim computes the geodesic distance to the goal for every candidate, so each sample carries the full action-distance vector and the best action ID.

Backtracking data generation: at ambiguous states (near-equal distances or certainty <0.1) the agent records the state, then revisits it after the episode to explore alternative viable paths. 54k raw trajectories are filtered with CLIP and loop rules to about 10k.
Compass-Data-SFT (11k): Qwen-QvQ-72B acts as teacher in habitat-sim; only successful episodes' <think>…</think><answer>k</answer> traces are kept, with no history frames in the input.
Stage 1 SFT: LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-VL-7B with cross-entropy on the whole reasoning-plus-action sequence, using masked softmax decoding so the chosen action index is always valid.

Stage 2 GRPO with gap-aware hybrid reward: r = softmax(-d/τ) base score + β_max·g·1[i=i*], where g = clip((d2-d1)/(|d1|+ε),0,1) is the certainty gap between the best and second-best actions. τ=0.5, β_max=1.0, G=5 rollouts, fixed KL to the SFT reference policy, ~170 steps.

Separate Stop Agent: an un-finetuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B decides whether to stop (within 1 m of the goal). A deterministic controller turns the chosen (r,θ) into move_forward 0.25 m and turn ±30° primitives.
Memory-agnostic design: history as text or concatenated images was tested and hurt performance, so the policy is trained without history and left open to external memory modules.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (LoRA SFT then GRPO RFT); Stop Agent is un-finetuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B
setting.training_data: Compass-Data-22k generated in habitat-sim on the HM3Dv2 train split: SFT 11k successful Qwen-QvQ-72B reasoning traces plus an RFT set of ~10k trajectories with full A* action-distance vectors
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with rendered action arrows (depth and pose used by the APM); goal is text category or goal image
setting.action_space: discrete high-level arrow candidates (r,θ) executed as low-level move_forward 0.25 m / turn ±30°, up to 500 steps, success radius 1 m
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle A* distances are used only for training data and rewards)

The NavNuances results (DC 82.54, NU 23.85, LR 59.92, RR 59.31, VM 22.94) are omitted because that benchmark is not in the canonical list.
results: CompassNav-7B reaches ObjNav SR/SPL 61.6/27.8 and InsImageNav 35.6/14.8, averaging 48.6/21.3. It beats GPT-4o (41.1/18.4) and o4-mini (46.5/20.1) on that average. Against modular methods it reaches 56.6 SR on HM3D versus UniGoal's 54.5, and 42.0 on MP3D versus 41.0. It also beats Nav-R1 on HM3D-OVON (43.5 vs 42.2 SR).
limitations: No history or memory is used; the paper acknowledges this and leaves external memory integration to future work, and SPL on HM3D (27.6) trails VLFM (30.4).
The 7B model is weak at numerical comprehension and instruction-following (NavNuances NU/DC below NavGPT-4V), and inference needs a remote H200 server.
Data generation requires oracle A* distances for every candidate at every step, which is costly, and a separate Stop Agent is needed. Real-world evidence is qualitative only.
